properties.areaDesc: San Francisco
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 23 at 6:10AM PST until November 26 at 4:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, Significant coastal
flooding with up to 2.7 feet of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.
For the High Surf Warning, Dangerously large breaking waves of
20 to 30 feet.

* WHERE...San Francisco County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 6 AM Monday to 4 PM
PST Thursday. For the High Surf Warning, from midnight Tuesday
night to midnight PST Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, numerous road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower
swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and
increasing the risk of drowning.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...These predictions are approaching the
highest tide ever recorded. At the San Francisco tide gauge,
high tide is expected to be 2.0 ft above normal (7.8 ft MLLW) at
9:25 AM Monday, 2.4 ft above normal (8.2 ft MLLW) at 10:05 AM
Tuesday, 2.7 ft above normal (8.5 ft MLLW) at 10:49 AM
Wednesday, and 2.2 ft above normal (8.0 ft MLLW) at 11:38 AM
Thursday. These predictions include up to 1.5 ft of surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High
tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific
Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other waterside
infrastructure.

properties.headline: Wind Advisory issued November 23 at 5:25AM PST until November 25 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Pendleton OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Dense Fog Advisory, visibility of one quarter mile
or less in dense fog and freezing fog. For the Wind Advisory for
the base and slopes of the northern Blue Mountains, southeast winds
25 to 35 mph with gusts of 40 to 55 mph expected.

* WHERE...Foothills of the Northern Blue Mountains of Oregon.

* WHEN...For the Dense Fog Advisory, until 11 AM PST this morning.
For the Wind Advisory, from 7 PM this evening to 4 AM PST
Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result. Low
visibility could make driving conditions hazardous.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Winds will be lighter away from the base of
the Blue Mountains.
properties.instruction:

profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

If driving, slow down, use your headlights, and leave plenty of
distance ahead of you.

properties.areaDesc: South Central Oregon Coast; Curry County Coast
properties.headline: High Wind Warning issued November 23 at 3:54AM PST until November 24 at 7:00PM PST by NWS Medford OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...South winds 25 to 40 mph with gusts up to 65 mph
expected.

* WHERE...Curry County Coast and South Central Oregon Coast,
including exposed areas of Highway 101.

* WHEN...From 4 PM today to 7 PM PST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Damaging winds will blow down trees and power lines.
Widespread power outages are expected. Travel will be
difficult, especially for high profile vehicles.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Winds are expected to be strongest late
Tuesday morning through early Tuesday afternoon. Wind gusts
could reach 75 mph on coastal headlands, including Cape Blanco
and Cape Sebastian.

* View the hazard area in detail at
https://www.wrh.noaa.gov/map/?wfo=mfr
properties.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

People are urged to secure loose objects, including large or
inflatable holiday decorations that could be blown around or
damaged by the wind.

properties.areaDesc: South Central Oregon Coast; Curry County Coast
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 23 at 3:52AM PST until November 26 at 7:00PM PST by NWS Medford OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, higher than normal
astronomical tides (King Tides) are expected to bring up to 2.4
ft of inundation above ground level in low-lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways today. For the Coastal Flood
Warning, higher than normal astronomical tides (King Tides)
combined with storm surge from large surf are expected to bring
up to 3.1 ft of inundation above ground level Tuesday and
Wednesday, with up to 2.6 ft of inundation expected on Thursday.
Additionally, storm surge from large breaking surf heights of
23 to 28 feet on Tuesday and Wednesday will add to already high
water levels.

* WHERE...Beaches and low lying areas along the shore lines of
Douglas, Coos and Curry Counties. This includes the
communities of North Bend, Charleston, Port Orford, Gold
Beach, and Coos Bay. Coastal flooding is expected to impact
portions of Highway 101 around Gold Beach, Coos Bay, and
Reedsport.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 7 AM to 4 PM PST
Monday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 7 AM Tuesday to 7
PM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. This
event is expected see similar impacts to what occurred on
January 3rd, 2026.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The worst conditions are expected to be
during the high tide periods in the late morning/early
afternoon. Storm activity lessens on Thursday, but King Tides
will still be present, which will likely continue inundation
impacts. At the Charleston, OR tide gauge, high tide is expected
to be at 10:09 AM today, at 10:51 AM Tuesday, at 11:35 AM
Wednesday, and at 12:23 PM Thursday.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

properties.areaDesc: Point Piedras Blancas to Point Sal westward out to 10 NM; East Santa Barbara Channel from Pt. Conception to Pt. Mugu CA including Santa Cruz Island
properties.headline: Marine Weather Statement issued November 23 at 3:27AM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
RISK OF BREAKING WAVES IN THE MORRO BAY AND VENTURA HARBOR
ENTRRANCES EARLY WEDNESDAY MORNING THROUGH THURSDAY AFTERNOON

A large and long period westerly swell will produce a risk of
breaking waves in the Morro Bay and Ventura Harbor entrances
early Wednesday morning through Thursday afternoon. These
conditions have a history of capsizing vessels of various sizes
resulting in serious injury or death, even to the most experienced
mariners.

Mariners are urged to stay clear of these harbor entrances during
the time mentioned. For more information, contact the local
harbor patrol or coast guard station and continue to monitor NOAA
Weather Radio for the latest weather information.

properties.areaDesc: Big Island Interior; Big Island Southeast
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 23 at 1:16AM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
properties.description:
Kilauea eruption episode 57 began at 12:15 AM HST this morning.
Lava fountain heights within Halemaumau Crater are currently
estimated at a few hundred feet high. The latest radar imagery has
detected small volcanic particles as high as 14,500 feet.
Light northerly surface winds near the volcano will push low level
particles towards the south of the crater. Winds aloft above the
low level boundary layer will blow from the northeast direction
pushing tephra towards the southwest direction.

We will continue to coordinate with USGS scientists on local ashfall
impacts as this latest Kilauea eruption and volcanic plume continues
to evolve over time.

Avoid excessive exposure to ash which is an eye and respiratory
irritant. Those with respiratory sensitivities should take extra
precaution to minimize exposure.

properties.areaDesc: San Diego County Coastal Areas; Orange County Coastal
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 23 at 2:36AM PST until November 27 at 1:00PM PST by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding
expected.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 AM PST Tuesday.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 4 AM Tuesday to 1 PM PST
Friday. Most susceptible time of flooding will be around the
time of the morning high tide, with peak tides trending from 7
AM on Monday to 10 AM on Friday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King tides peak Tuesday through Wednesday
at 7.9-8.3 feet, likely breaking the all-time tidal records set
back in late October. Background surf on top of the tides will
remain around 2-5 feet through Wednesday, but a long period west
swell arriving late Wednesday will bring much larger surf by
Thursday morning's high tide. Breaking waves may reach 6-8 feet
with sets up to 10-12 feet on west-facing beaches. Surf lowers
to 3-6 feet by Friday.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

inches.

* WHERE...Iron County.

* WHEN...Until 10 AM CST this morning.

* IMPACTS...Plan on slippery road conditions. The hazardous
conditions will impact the Monday morning commute.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Blustery northwest winds gusting 20 to 25 mph
combined with falling snow may cause visibility to fall below 1
mile at times during the Monday morning commute.
properties.instruction:

www.511wi.gov for Wisconsin road information.

Lake effect snow bands and showers are expected to create conditions
ranging from locally heavy snow to dry weather just a few miles away.
Visibilities can also vary greatly. Be prepared for rapid changes in
weather, visibility, and road conditions.

properties.description:

steep seas 12 to 14 ft at 13 seconds through tonight. South
winds increase late tonight to gales 30 to 40 kt with gusts up
to 50 kt with very steep and hazardous seas 18 to 23 ft at 12
seconds expected. South winds increase again late Monday night
with storm force winds of 40 to 50 kt with gusts 55 to 60 kt.
Seas will become very steep and chaotic 23 to 28 ft at 13
seconds.

* WHERE...All areas.

* WHEN...For the Small Craft Advisory, until 7 AM PST Monday.
For the Gale Warning, from 7 AM Monday to 4 AM PST Tuesday.
For the Storm Warning, from 4 AM to 4 PM PST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Very strong winds and very steep seas could capsize
or damage vessels. Visibilities will be significantly reduced.
properties.instruction:
Mariners should remain in port, alter course, and/or secure the
vessel for very strong winds and very steep and hazardous seas.

capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility.

recommended that mariners without the proper experience seek safe
harbor prior to the onset of gale conditions.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Watch issued November 22 at 10:49PM PST until November 26 at 2:00PM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Watch, High astronomical tides
and large surf with storm surge may cause moderate flooding in
low lying areas along the Redwood/Mendocino Coast. Up to one
foot of saltwater inundation above ground level is possible in
low lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Coastal Del Norte, Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal
Mendocino Counties.

* WHEN...From Tuesday morning through Thursday afternoon during
periods of high tide.

* IMPACTS...Several coastal roads may be closed. Low lying
property and some critical infrastructure will be inundated.
Some shoreline erosion may occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Expect continued increases in high tide
water levels through the coming work week with the tide
peaking on Wednesday. Prepare now and pay attention to
official guidance on shelters and or resources available to
the public.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Watch means that flooding is possible but not
imminent. Coastal residents in the watch area should begin
preparations for rising water and take appropriate action to
protect life and property.

Feet Above Ground is locally defined as feet above the Highest
Astronomical Tide or HAT.

surge may cause moderate flooding in low lying areas along the

above ground level is possible in low lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways.

Monday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Monday afternoon
through Thursday afternoon. High tide is at 9:44 AM at the
Humboldt Bay North Spit tide gauge. Saltwater inundation will
be possible 1 to 2 hours before and after high tide.

property and some critical infrastructure will be inundated.

King Salmon and the Arcata bottoms/sections of highway 101

forecast.

marinas along the river and in the Hontoon Island area.

- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 6.1 feet late this
week. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 4.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

high tide level. No flooding is expected.

properties.areaDesc: Mason, WA
properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued November 22 at 3:44PM PST by NWS Seattle WA
properties.description:
ESFSEW

A series of weather systems will bring heavy precipitation to the
Olympic Peninsula starting this week. Snow levels will rise to around
5000 feet or higher, allowing this to be primarily in the form of
rain from Tuesday onward. This will bring 3 to 4 inches of rain to
the Olympics this week, leading to significant rises on the Skokomish
River in Mason County. Any snowfall in the upper portions of the
basin through Monday will likely add to additional runoff. Flooding
is currently expected as early as late Wednesday and may continue
until the weekend.

Please monitor the latest river forecasts from the National Weather
Service for additional information.

properties.areaDesc: Mason, WA
properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued November 22 at 3:21PM PST by NWS Seattle WA
properties.description:
ESFSEW

A series of weather systems will bring heavy precipitation to the
Olympic Peninsula starting this week. Snow levels will rise to around
5000 feet or higher, allowing this to be primarily in the form of
rain from Tuesday onward. This will bring 3 to 4 inches of rain to
the Olympics this week, leading to significant rises on the Skokomish
River in Mason County. Any snowfall in the upper portions of the
basin through Monday will likely add to additional runoff. Flooding
is currently expected as early as late Wednesday and may continue
until the weekend.

Please monitor the latest river forecasts from the National Weather
Service for additional information.

* WHERE...Central Yuma County in southwestern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 315 PM MST Friday Nov 27.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is expected. Low-water crossings are
likely to become inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 313 PM MST, a streamflow gauge has indicated that water from
an upstream dam release from Painted Rock Dam has reached
Dateland. Flooding is expected along the Gila River within the
warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Farmlands and low-water crossings along the Gila River.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.
